messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & proposed term/capacity changes for Metrik — please review

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our sync, I’m sending a proposed renewal structure for Metrik that balances predictability for you and runway for the capacity uplift you’re asking for. High-level: 

- Term: propose shifting to an 18‑month renewal (instead of 12) with a mid-term pricing true-up at month 12.
- Capacity: move from 250M token quota/month to a staged uplift: 350M month 1–6, 500M month 7–18.
- Pricing: blended unit price for the first 6 months (intro uplift) then a reduced committed rate for months 7–18.
- SLA: standard Redwood SLA with a request to keep credit cap at 10% of monthly spend (we can discuss exceptions).

Attached: Metrik_Renewal_Proposal_rafael_v1.pdf (proposal + draft order form).

Could you send back any redlines your team has (legal + procurement) and flag hard blockers? If feasible, we’d like to lock terms the week of 7/20 so we can provision the dedicated capacity pool.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147
From: Elena Morales <elena@metrik.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@metrik.ai, legal@metrik.ai
Date: 2026-07-13T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & proposed term/capacity changes for Metrik — please review

Rafael —

Thanks for the proposal. We reviewed it internally and have marked up a set of redlines — main concerns below: 

1) Data retention: we cannot agree to the proposed 365‑day retention of request/response logs. Our security policy requires a maximum of 90 days; please advise whether Redwood can accommodate or whether we need a narrow carve for diagnostics.
2) Indemnity & regulatory scope: the indemnity language needs clarification around third‑party data and regulated workloads.
3) Burst/billing: the staged uplift is fine, but procurement wants clearer language on burst overage pricing and how we get visibility into burst usage.
4) SLA credits: we requested a higher single‑incident credit threshold for enterprise outages (we proposed 20% in the doc).

Attached: Metrik_Redlines_MetrikLegal_v1.docx (tracked changes + comments). I’ve copied procurement and legal — they’ll follow up on specific redlines.

Best,
Elena
VP Product Operations | Metrik
Elena.Morales@metrik.ai

Neha / Karthik —

Forwarding Metrik’s redlines (attached). Quick notes / ask: 

- Data retention: customer insists on 90 days. Can we propose 90 days for PII/production logs and 180 days for ephemeral diagnostic logs, with access controls and export hooks? If not, what’s our risk profile for 90 days?
- Indemnity: they flagged third‑party/regulatory carveouts. Please propose language that preserves Redwood IP protections but narrows broad third‑party exposure.
- Burst pricing: propose we add a transparent burst rate table to the order form and a monthly burst cap toggle (they can opt in). Karthik, can you confirm technical feasibility and whether we need a lead time to provision additional GPUs?

I’ve drafted two starter lines in Draft_Counterlanguage_neha_v1.docx — please iterate and send back a consolidated counter by EOD 7/17 so we can aim for signature the week of 7/20.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Metrik redlines — proposed counter + next steps

Rafael / Karthik / Elena —

Thanks for the redlines, Elena, and for looping us in. I reviewed Metrik_Redlines_MetrikLegal_v1.docx and prepared a narrow counterproposal (attached: Draft_Counterlanguage_neha_v1.docx) summarizing the changes we can accept and the areas that need an escalated conversation. Summary of the key points we can take today: 

- Data retention: Redwood will accept a 90‑day retention window for production request/response logs with the following guardrails: (a) logs are encrypted at rest; (b) access is limited to named roles and requires justification; (c) Redwood will provide an export of retained logs on a 7‑day SLA for audit requests. For diagnostic traces (non‑PII), Redwood requests 180‑day retention to assist with model regressions; we’re open to an auditable retention policy and can add a retention toggle in the private deployment plan.

- Indemnity: we will narrow third‑party exposure and remove language that implies broad coverage for customer‑caused misuse. We will keep standard IP protections intact. See tracked changes in the attached.

- Burst / billing: proposed addition to the order form — a transparent tiered burst rate table plus an optional monthly burst cap (default off). If Metrik enables the cap, overages beyond the cap will be quoted and require 7 days’ notice to provision burst capacity.

- SLA credits: we can accept a higher credit for enterprise outages (up to 15%) but cannot extend to 20% without exec approval. If 20% is a hard requirement, I’ll escalate to Legal/Finance and loop in Marissa for approval.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm acceptance of the 90/180 retention split and the 15% SLA credit.
2) If accepted, I’ll incorporate the final language into RF_OrderForm_v3.pdf and initiate DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/XYZ-123-sign
Attached: Draft_Counterlanguage_neha_v1.docx, RF_OrderForm_v3.pdf

If all looks good, Rafael — please confirm and I’ll send the DocuSign packet.

Best,
